title: Question 12
stem: The Sun has luminosity $L = 3.83 \times 10^{26}\text{ W}$ and radius $r = 6.96 \times 10^8\text{ m}$. The Earth orbits the Sun at distance $d = 1.51 \times 10^{11}\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (a)

markscheme_points.text: total power of radiation emitted (by a star / object)

hints: State the definition of stellar luminosity in terms of radiated power.

walkthrough: Define stellar luminosity: total power of radiation emitted (by the star).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the radiant flux intensity $F$ of the Sun at the Earth.
hints: Apply the inverse-square law for radiant flux intensity: $F = \frac{L}{4\pi d^2}$.
Substitute $L = 3.83 \times 10^{26}\text{ W}$ and $d = 1.51 \times 10^{11}\text{ m}$, and state the unit $\text{W m}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Use radiant flux formula: $F = \frac{L}{4\pi d^2}$.

Substitute values: $F = \frac{3.83 \times 10^{26}\text{ W}}{4\pi \times (1.51 \times 10^{11}\text{ m})^2} = \frac{3.83 \times 10^{26}}{2.865 \times 10^{23}} = 1336.8\text{ W m}^{-2} \approx 1340\text{ W m}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the mass lost by the Sun per second as radiation.
hints: Energy emitted per second is equal to the luminosity $L = 3.83 \times 10^{26}\text{ J s}^{-1}$.
Apply $E = mc^2 \implies m = \frac{L}{c^2}$.
walkthrough: Rate of energy loss: $E = 3.83 \times 10^{26}\text{ J}$ per second.

Mass lost per second: $m = \frac{E}{c^2} = \frac{3.83 \times 10^{26}\text{ J}}{(3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1})^2} = \frac{3.83 \times 10^{26}}{9.00 \times 10^{16}} = 4.256 \times 10^9\text{ kg} \approx 4.26 \times 10^9\text{ kg}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Use the Stefan-Boltzmann law to show that the surface temperature $T$ of the Sun is $5770\text{ K}$.
hints: Use the Stefan-Boltzmann law for star luminosity: $L = 4\pi r^2 \sigma T^4$.
Substitute $L = 3.83 \times 10^{26}\text{ W}$, $r = 6.96 \times 10^8\text{ m}$, and $\sigma = 5.67 \times 10^{-8}\text{ W m}^{-2}\text{ K}^{-4}$ and solve for $T$.
walkthrough: Write Stefan-Boltzmann law: $L = 4\pi \sigma r^2 T^4 \implies T = \left(\frac{L}{4\pi \sigma r^2}\right)^{1/4}$.
Substitute: $3.83 \times 10^{26} = 4\pi \times (5.67 \times 10^{-8}) \times (6.96 \times 10^8)^2 \times T^4 = 3.454 \times 10^{11} \times T^4$.
Compute: $T^4 = 1.1088 \times 10^{15} \implies T = 5771\text{ K} \approx 5770\text{ K}$.

Substitute: $3.83 \times 10^{26} = 4\pi \times (5.67 \times 10^{-8}) \times (6.96 \times 10^8)^2 \times T^4 = 3.454 \times 10^{11} \times T^4$.
Compute: $T^4 = 1.1088 \times 10^{15} \implies T = 5771\text{ K} \approx 5770\text{ K}$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: The Sun will eventually expand into a red giant with lower surface temperature. State and explain the change in the spectrum of thermal radiation emitted by the Sun.

markscheme_points.text: peak wavelength shifts to longer wavelength / lower frequency according to Wien displacement law
intensity at each wavelength / total power per unit area decreases

hints: Apply Wien's displacement law: $\lambda_{\text{max}} T = \text{constant}$, so $\lambda_{\text{Sirius}} T_{\text{Sirius}} = \lambda_{\text{Sun}} T_{\text{Sun}}$.
Substitute $\lambda_{\text{Sun}} = 5.00 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$, $T_{\text{Sun}} = 5770\text{ K}$, and $T_{\text{Sirius}} = 9940\text{ K}$.
walkthrough: From Wien's displacement law: $\lambda_{\text{max}} \propto \frac{1}{T} \implies \lambda_{\text{Sirius}} = \lambda_{\text{Sun}} \times \frac{T_{\text{Sun}}}{T_{\text{Sirius}}}$.
Substitute: $\lambda_{\text{Sirius}} = (5.00 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}) \times \frac{5770\text{ K}}{9940\text{ K}} = 2.9024 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \approx 2.90 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$.
